newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian central bank cuts key refinancing rate.
newsitem.headline: Latvian central bank cuts key refinancing rate.

text.p: The Latvian central bank on Monday said it has cut its key refinancing rate to 10 percent per annum from 11 percent and said the reduction was due to falling inflation and healthier government finances.
The rate is an important reference rate in the Latvian money market and is the minimum rate at which banks can obtain two-week funds from the central bank.

Banks can also obtain overnight funds at the refinancing rate plus three percent. The central bank said in a statement that inflation has fallen further since the last cut on September 13, which was from 12 percent to 11 percent.
"At the same time, interbank market activity has continually grown and money market interest rates have fallen, showing the stability of Latvia's financial markets," the bank said.
Latvia's financial situation has gone on a more even keel since a banking crisis hit it in the middle of 1995.
Rates on government Treasury bills have been falling continously and the government has decided that the 1997 budget will be balanced, after a 40 million lat deficit planned for this year.
